newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Afghan Taleban commander said killed in fighting.
newsitem.headline: Afghan Taleban commander said killed in fighting.

text.p: A senior commander of Afghanistan's radical Islamic Taleban militia, Mullah Abdul Ahad, was killed in fighting with former government forces north of Kabul, Taleban sources said on Monday.
The sources, contacted from Pakistan, did not say when Ahad had been killed. No other details were immediately available.
The Taleban were preparing to defend the Afghan capital on Monday after suffering military setbacks north of the city at the hands of ousted government commander Ahmad Shah Masood.
The Pakistan-based Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) quoted witnesses in the eastern city of Jalalabad as saying that many Taleban casualties had been ferried to the hospital there.

"We have seen lots of wounded and there are not enough beds for them, so they are lying in the corridors," one witness said. "Lightly wounded fighters are being discharged, but at least 15 seriously wounded cases have been transferred to Pakistan."
Foreign aid workers based in Islamabad and Peshawar could not immediately confirm the report.
AIP said Taleban leaders had asked local commanders in Jalalabad and the surrounding province of Nangarhar to prepare fresh fighters to be sent to frontlines near Kabul.

The Taleban captured Kabul on September 27 and pushed north to bottle up Masood's forces in his Panjsher Valley stronghold. But Masood's battle-hardened guerrillas have since retaken his old headquarters at Jabal os-Siraj and pushed the Taleban most of the way back to the capital in the past two days.
